name: Ruby
summary: A dynamic object-oriented language runtime organized around object-valued data, late-bound methods, VM execution contexts, garbage collection, and a C extension boundary.

features.name: Dynamic object and method model
features.description: Ruby values are objects whose methods can be defined on classes, modules, and individual objects. Method lookup, singleton methods, and overriding are runtime-visible parts of the language model.
benefits: Supports late-bound polymorphism and object-specific behavior
Provides flexible composition through classes, modules, and method definitions
costs: Runtime method changes complicate static reasoning and optimization
Dispatch behavior depends on mutable object and class state

features.name: VM frame and fiber execution contexts
features.description: The MRI implementation represents execution through VM stack frames and supports fibers as resumable execution contexts. The fixed source contains VM and thread execution code used to manage calls and execution state.
benefits: Makes call state and resumable computation explicit runtime boundaries
Supports cooperative decomposition of work without requiring an OS process per unit
costs: Frame, fiber, and thread lifecycle rules increase runtime complexity
Concurrency behavior depends on the selected execution context and implementation constraints

features.name: Garbage-collected object lifetime
features.description: Ruby manages ordinary object reachability through its garbage collector and exposes GC control and observation APIs. The fixed source contains the collector implementation and object-marking machinery.
benefits: Removes ordinary manual reclamation from Ruby-level object management
Lets the runtime determine reachability across object graphs
costs: Collection work and heap behavior remain runtime concerns
Native integrations must preserve the collector's reachability assumptions

features.name: GC-managed C extension boundary
features.description: Ruby exposes objects to C extensions through the VALUE representation and requires extension code to use the runtime API. Typed native data supplies mark, free, size, and compaction callbacks that participate in object lifetime management.
benefits: Allows native libraries to participate in the Ruby object model
Defines explicit hooks for native data reachability and cleanup
costs: Extensions must obey VALUE typing and garbage-collector reachability rules
Native callbacks and runtime object access add embedding and reentrancy constraints

mathematical_views.model: Dynamic object graph with late-bound dispatch
mathematical_views.question: How do object identity, class/module membership, and mutable method definitions determine a method call?
assumptions: Objects and classes are vertices and references or lookup relations are edges
A method call is modeled as a lookup transition followed by execution
Inline caches and JIT details are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: How do calls, frames, fibers, and threads transition while Ruby code runs and suspends?
assumptions: Execution contexts have a current frame and may suspend or resume at defined boundaries
The model distinguishes language-level resumability from OS scheduling
The view describes MRI evidence and does not claim that all Ruby implementations share its internal layout

mathematical_views.question: How does Ruby determine which managed objects remain live and when native wrapped data can be released?
assumptions: Managed objects are vertices and references are directed reachability edges
Collector phases are abstract transitions over the reachable subgraph
The model excludes collector timing, heap layout, and implementation-specific pause behavior

costs: Mutable dispatch state increases analysis and optimization cost
Suspension and scheduling rules complicate lifecycle reasoning

benefits: Automatic object reclamation based on runtime reachability
costs: Heap and collection behavior are runtime-managed rather than directly scheduled by application code

benefits: Native interoperability within managed lifetime rules
costs: C extensions carry strict ownership, marking, and reentrancy obligations
